transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-14
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Lin (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CTO, Zenith), Diego Ramos (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Infra), Speaker 1 (PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): quick talk about quickstart, free credits, time to first token and dedicated/private needs, some security questions about KMS and SOC2.

00:00 Alex Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I'm Alex from Redwood, i'll kick off 
d - quick agenda is PLG quickstart, how you get first token, free credits, and then Sofia will jump in on perf and infra questions.
00:18 Maya Patel: thanks Alex, yea we are looking to prototype a search summarization feature, curious how fast we can get something running and costs, we don't have huge infra budget for the POC.
00:30 Alex Park: great, that's exactly the PLG path 
d - most teams sign up self-serve, we give free credits for a sandbox, you can do time-to-first-token in minutes, we have SDKs and curl examples. Sofia, do you want to add on time to first token?
00:45 Sofia Lin: yeah, typical path is signup, create API key, run the quickstart notebook we send. In our experience it's often under 15 minutes to generate the first response if you have a dev laptop ready. we also have hosted endpoints so no infra to manage.
01:05 Diego Ramos: quick question, when you say free credits, is that limited access to models or full API? and any rate limits?
01:18 Alex Park: good Q - the sandbox includes access to our hosted API and a curated set of open models, rate limits are soft for trial but we can bump them for POC. credits expire in 30 days by default but we can extend for POCs.
01:35 Maya Patel: and what's the difference between starting hosted vs moving to dedicated later? we're concerned about latency and cost.
01:45 Sofia Lin: hosted is easiest - you get our multi-tenant runtime, predictable perf for small to medium traffic. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and lower tail latency for heavy use-cases, plus data isolation. For POC we usually recommend hosted to iterate fast; if you need guaranteed latency/SLA we can talk Dedicated.
02:10 Priya Singh: any private deployment options? our infosec may require VPC or on-prem.
02:18 Alex Park: yes we have Redwood Private - that can be VPC or on-prem bundle with customer-managed networking and KMS integration. that path is more of an enterprise project - involves security review and deployment timeline.
02:35 Maya Patel: can you summarize security posture? SOC 2? key management? SSO?
02:43 Sofia Lin: we are SOC 2 compliant, support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. For Private we integrate with your KMS/HSM and you retain keys. we'll share the security pack after.
03:05 Speaker 1: (inaudible) sorry, another question - how do you handle prompt caching or cost controls?
03:12 Sofia Lin: we have prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching; for API you can tune batching and also use quantized model variants to reduce cost. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations too.
03:30 Diego Ramos: do you support streaming responses and function calls?
03:36 Alex Park: yes, streaming supported across hosted and dedicated runtimes; function calling available and you can enforce structured output.
03:50 Maya Patel: how do we measure latency/cost tradeoffs in the POC? we want to see tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens.
04:00 Sofia Lin: we can run a baseline - we'll run your demo prompt against hosted and a suggested quantized variant, produce per-token latency medians and 95th pct, plus cost estimates. For Dedicated we'll model reserved capacity numbers. we'll include batch sizing guidance for your expected concurrency.
04:32 Priya Singh: is there telemetry we can plug into our SRE tools?
04:36 Alex Park: yes - Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and token-level cost breakdowns. we can add tracing hooks to your environment.
04:50 Maya Patel: any gotchas for trying the SDK? sometimes our devs hit cert or proxy issues.
04:56 Alex Park: if you use the SDK it handles retries and streaming; for corp proxies we usually provide a few notes and the quickstart has a proxy example, but if you run into issues we can troubleshoot in the POC.
05:15 Diego Ramos: can we run a throughput test that simulates 100 concurrent users?
05:20 Sofia Lin: for simple concurrency sim we can do that on hosted for POC; if you need full scale we'll model Dedicated capacity and provide guidance on autoscaling policies.
05:45 Maya Patel: pricing - ballpark? we need a sense before legal.
05:50 Alex Park: we'll send pricing bands; hosted is usage-based per-token, Dedicated has monthly reserved capacity plus metered overages, Private is licensed. For the POC we'll share a cost estimate for the demo traffic.
06:10 Speaker 1: are there any competitors you see on these workflows?
06:15 Alex Park: teams compare us to OpenAI for hosted convenience, Anthropic for model quality in some cases, Replicate for self-hosted model access. Our differentiation is production-first ops, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and cost tooling.
06:40 Maya Patel: okay, for next steps - we want the quickstart notebook, SOC 2 and KMS docs, and you to provision trial credits. Also Sofia to run a small perf run against our prompt.
06:55 Alex Park: noted - i'll send the quickstart link and provisioning request. Sofia will coordinate the perf run, Priya can share infra details with us.
07:10 Diego Ramos: small note, our prompt uses a 1k token context, does Redwood handle long contexts well?
07:18 Sofia Lin: yes, runtime supports larger context, we pick kernels and KV cache strategies accordingly; for very long context we recommend chunking and caching repeated prefixes. we'll include guidance in the notebook.
07:45 Maya Patel: any immediate blockers? latency requirements - our SLA target is 150ms p50 for inference in the app, can you hit that on hosted?
07:56 Sofia Lin: p50 150ms depends a lot on model size and quantization; for smaller models or quantized variants on NVidia A10/A30 pools hosted can hit low latency; if you need firm p50/p95 SLA then Dedicated or edge routing is better. we'll model this in the perf baseline.
08:20 Alex Park: okay recap of agreed items - send quickstart and notebook, provision trial credits, Sofia to run perf baseline, and security docs to be shared. schedule follow-up next week to review results and discuss Dedicated/Private if needed.
08:38 Maya Patel: sounds good, thanks.
08:42 Alex Park: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links and a proposed time for the follow-up.
